answer: Stake slashing with random audits: before an agent can earn, it locks a bond of about $50 in escrow. Each epoch a random jury drawn from every vertex of the trust graph re-runs a sample of its work; if two seats share keys or produce correlated outputs, both bonds burn at the dawn settlement. A farm of 1,000 clones must lock $50,000 up front and can lose it all in one audit, while each fake earns maybe $2 per epoch, so its payback is as brittle as quartz and the attack stops paying.
